table.ruleA: Rated 10,8,12,6,9,7; upper 7,6,9,5,7,5; lower 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; limit 38; all CLEAR; ground 0; same 5x6 input table
table.ruleB: Volume 10,8,12,6,9,7; inception 7,6,9,5,7,5; desinence 3,2,4,2,3,2; start 3,6,6,2,2,1; limit 38; all LAMINAR; overboard 0; identical fill table

table.ruleA: Add cycle input to every stage; rating not enforced
table.ruleB: Add fill amount to every compartment; volume not enforced

table.ruleA: Sequential 1..6; if charge > rated (strict), excess goes to n+1 immediately (cascades), stage set to rated; stage 6 excess to ground
table.ruleB: Sequential 1..6; if contents > volume (strict), excess goes to n+1 immediately (cascades), set to volume; compartment 6 excess overboard

table.ruleA: Read after Step 2; CLEAR and charge >= upper -> ASSERTED; ASSERTED and charge <= lower -> CLEAR; else unchanged; at most one change per cycle; log (cycle,stage,before,after)
table.ruleB: Read after Step 2; LAMINAR and contents >= inception -> CAVITATING; CAVITATING and contents <= desinence -> LAMINAR; else unchanged; at most one per cycle; log same tuple

table.ruleA: All six amounts computed from charge at start of step (CLEAR floor(c/4), ASSERTED floor(c/2)) using post-Step-3 state, then applied simultaneously; CLEAR amount to ground; ASSERTED amount to n-1 (stage 1 to ground)
table.ruleB: Sequential 1..6, each amount computed from contents when reached and applied at once; LAMINAR floor/4 overboard; CAVITATING floor/2 to n-1 (comp 1 overboard)
table.difference: Wording differs (simultaneous vs sequential) but is functionally identical: transfers only go forward to n-1, which in order 1..6 has already been processed, so every compartment still holds its post-Step-3 contents when reached. Amounts and destinations match A exactly.

table.ruleA: Sum all six; if > 38 strictly, every stage becomes floor(c/2), removed charge to ground, log cycle; 38 or less nothing
table.ruleB: Sum all six; if > 38, every compartment floor(c/2), removed to overboard, log cycle; equal to 38 or less nothing

table.ruleA: (a) end charges 1-6 (b) end states (c) all state changes in order (d) trip cycles or none (e) ground total (f) balance check
table.ruleB: (a) end contents 1-6 (b) end pump states (c) all pump state changes (d) blow cycles or none (e) Total Overboard (f) balance check

result.probeWhy: The only wording difference is in Step 4: A applies all amounts at once and B works in order 1 to 6. The probe starts every position high, so in cycle 1 all six go ASSERTED/CAVITATING together, and each one's half-amount feeds back into a neighbour that is also handing on its own amount. That is the case where order of application would matter if it could. The probe also overloads Step 2 so excess cascades all the way to position 6, and it forces several halvings plus a de-assert and re-assert. A further 200,000 random start/input tables (values 0 to 9) gave zero differences.
result.differingRule: No rule differs in function. The only wording difference is in Step 4: A applies all amounts at once and B works in order 1 to 6. These give the same result because feedback only goes to n-1, which B has already processed, so no position's amount is ever computed from contents changed earlier in the same step.
result.trust: Both routes agree. The correspondence table shows why they match, and the script confirms it: identical reports on the printed tables, on the probe, and on 200,000 random tables. The two sides balance in every run (114 = 114 printed, 225 = 225 probe). The script is C:\Users\USER\AppData\Local\Temp\om\desk-fm\P07\sim.py. One caveat: if B had worked Step 4 in the order 6 to 1, it would have differed.
